before: An ordered session sent each new picture to the room as blob frames: base64 chunks of at most 512 KiB on the room's socket. The room put the chunks together, checked them, stored them, and answered blob-stored or blob-refused (with blob-order for a chunk out of order). The protocol version was 1.
after: An ordered session gives each new picture to the host's upload option (OrderedCollaborationOptions.upload), four at a time, with the place welcome.blobs names, the hash, the content type, the bytes and a signal the session aborts when it ends. The host stores it over its own link, for example an HTTP PUT. A change that names the picture waits until the upload says it is stored; a refusal (blob-too-large, blob-hash, blob-type, blob-quota) takes the change back by name; a rejected upload goes again after the reconnect delays and at once after a rejoin. The protocol has no blob, blob-stored or blob-refused message, no blob-order code, and is version 2. The room still refuses a change whose media its storage does not hold (missing-blob).
reason: The Yjs document format does not change. The ordered protocol does: a page and a room of different versions refuse each other's frames by name (invalid-version, reload: version), and an ordered room admits only clients of its own code version, so the room server and its pages always move together. Change messages, the change log and its kinds keep their meaning. Ordered rooms are not deployed yet, so no room or page uses blob frames and no migration is needed.
